name: Pear
grown_as: Fruit trees on rootstocks: dessert pears ('Williams' (dwarf), 'Doyenné du Comice', 'Cornishgold', 'Zoete Brederode', 'Strawberry Pear') and perry pears ('Beetroot Wick Court Alex', 'Merrylegs', 'Dead Boy', 'Green Horse'), which share the drawing. Perry pear trees grow far taller and their fruit is often small and rounder.
habit: A deciduous tree with a narrower, more upright crown than an apple, the branches rising steeply; 3 to 5 m on Quince rootstock, perry pear standards 10 to 15 m or more. Bark grey-brown, breaking into small square plates on older trees. Fruits on spurs like apple.

leaf.arrangement: Alternate; in tufts on the spurs
leaf.outline: Broadly oval to almost round, 5 to 8 cm long
leaf.margin: Very finely and bluntly toothed all round, the teeth so small the edge can look smooth
leaf.veins: A pale midrib and 5 to 8 pairs of fine side veins curving forward
leaf.surface: Glossy, smooth and hairless when grown; paler and duller beneath
leaf.stalk: Long and slender, 2 to 5 cm, often as long as half the blade, so the leaves flutter
leaf.colour: Rich, shiny dark green; yellow to red or black-purple in autumn

flower.form: An open flat flower, smaller and flatter than apple blossom
flower.petals: Five, free, round, with a short claw, not touching
flower.centre: About twenty stamens with dark red-purple anthers (turning blackish when spent), around five free pale styles
flower.carried: In rounded clusters of five to ten on longish stalks at the spur tips, opening just before or with the leaves
flower.season: April, a week or two before apple

fruit: A pome, pear-shaped: broad at the bottom and narrowing towards a long stalk that is not sunk in a hollow; the dried sepals at the bottom. 6 to 12 cm on dessert pears (perry pears 3 to 6 cm and often round). Green ripening yellow-green, often with brown russet patches or a red blush ('Williams' yellow with a faint blush, 'Comice' yellow-green with russet). Hangs on its long stalk. Ripe August to October. Fruit set: small green fruitlets on long stalks in clusters, the sepals at the tip.
seedling: Not drawn: grown as grafted trees
winter: Bare tree with steeply rising branches. Spurs carry plump, pointed, shiny brown flower buds; buds on the shoots slender, pointed and standing away from the stem.

leaf: roundish oval leaf on a long slender stalk
margin very finely toothed, almost smooth
bloom: five round pure white petals with gaps between
dark red-purple anthers in the centre
young: glossy oval leaves on long stalks
flower: clusters of pure white blossom with dark centres on the spurs
flowers with or just before the leaves
set: small green fruitlets in clusters at the spur tips
each on a long slender stalk, dried sepals at the tip
crop: pear-shaped fruit narrowing to the stalk
fruit hanging on long stalks, yellow-green with russet or a blush

look_alikes: Apple blossom is pink-backed with yellow anthers, its leaves downy beneath on shorter stalks. Wild pear (Pyrus pyraster) is thorny with small hard fruit. Quince has single large pale pink flowers and woolly leaves with smooth edges.
